title: Derivative expectation on a biased sign cube
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p_i\in(0,1)$ for each $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and choose a sign vector $X\in\{-1,1\}^n$ with independent coordinates, where $\mathbb{P}(X_i=1)=1-p_i$ and $\mathbb{P}(X_i=-1)=p_i$. For any real-valued function $f$ on the sign cube, coordinate $i$, and sign $b\in\{-1,1\}$, the expectation of its discrete derivative in coordinate $i$ times the indicator of $X_i=b$ equals the probability of that sign times the expectation of the derivative; that probability is $1-p_i$ if $b=1$ and $p_i$ if $b=-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube
